newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo 64-bit player shipments reach 4 mln units.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo 64-bit player shipments reach 4 mln units.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Thursday that worldwide shipments of its 64-bit home-use game player reached about four million units by the end of 1996. The Nintendo 64 player was launched in June.
Nintendo expects global shipments of the player to reach a total of some six million units by the end of March, a company spokesman said.
Nintendo started selling the player in Japan on June 23 last year and in North America on September 29.
Sales are expected to start in Europe on March 1.
By the end of last year, shipments in North America had reached 2.14 million units while shipments in Japan totalled 1.85 million units, the Nintendo spokesman said.
By the end of March, the company expects 3.0 to 3.2 million shipments in North America, 2.1 million to 2.3 million in Japan, and 500,000 to 900,000 in Europe, the spokesman said.
But he added total shipments would be limited by output constraints.
"As our production capacity is limited, it would be difficult to increase our shipments further," the spokesman said.
